summary: Necrotising fasciitis in patient injecting drugs.
Several areas reporting increase in alcohol use in patients presenting to drug services.
Overdose (collapse, seizures, confusion) on a street after taking a handful of pills 15 minutes prior. Acquaintances also under the influence stated they had taken fentanyl tablets.

Overdose after using a half of a tenner bag of heroin (more beige than usual). Had chest pains and could feel 'scratchy hot feeling as it was making its way from the site of injection'. Reports the drugs felt different and stronger than normal.

area: Greater Glasgow and Clyde, South Lanarkshire
summary: Multiple overdoses and deaths reported in Greater Glasgow and Clyde and Lanarkshire. All linked to drugs sold as heroin.
Communication sent to pharmacies in response to reports of the use of lean (made by combining codeine, antihistamines and sweet drinks).
Manchester Drug Analysis Exchange (MANDRAKE) detected xylazine in three out of four samples of ketamine tested in Manchester in one week.
Adverse effects including complete memory loss, agitation and aggression.

Acute poisonings associated with drugs sold as alprazolam and Xanax containing protonitazene. Other symptoms include loss of consciousness, altered mental state, collapse, unconsciousness and respiratory arrest.
Report to service of adulterated cocaine causing adverse effects including decreased energy, difficulty breathing and 'feeling heavy'.
Adverse effects including confusion, decreased energy and nausea after taking heroin. Reportedly 'very high potency'.
Multiple reports of black tar heroin being sold as heroin, reported to be potent and sold in small quantities. Adverse effects include prolonged periods of unconsciousness.
Multiple reports of people losing time (two hours) after injecting heroin. Effects of heroin 'not like anything they had before'.

Overdose after taking two 10mg Zimovane pills. White pills with half score on one side. Sourced from a dealer in strips of 14 for £1-2 per pill. Believes them to be fake or 'street Zimovane' due to them being 10mg (they can normally only get them as 3.5 or 7.5mg). Also taken gabapentin and methadone.
Overdose on a street. Patient was found with two empty, six-tablet, diazepam blister packets (one 2mg and one 5mg), as well as one white round tablet marked with '10'.
Adverse effects including feeling pain all over their body and back and was feeling very cold, 13 hours after injecting 'heroin, fentanyl, cocaine and Valium into both upper arms'.
Reports of young people snorting a drug called 'the pink stuff' or 'pink cocaine' reported to contain ketamine, LSD and amphetamine.

Overdose (collapse) from injecting heroin powder from a new dealer that was more pinkish than normal beige. Adverse effects including seizures and loss of consciousness. Also bought blue benzos that were bigger than usual.

Multiple patients with acute liver failure after taking anabolic steroids. One patient was reported to be taking red circular pills from a white bottle labelled 'Advar UK Labs, Dianabol, methandrostenolone, 50mg tablets'. This is a high dose (an average dose is 10mg). The drug was confirmed by testing as containing methandrostenolone.

Client reporting person taking 14+ Ksalols in blister packs on a number of occasions and overdosed as a result of this. Naloxone had minimal effect. Person sourced pills from a dealer and felt that the tablets were stronger than they have had previously.
Drug overdose and death in close proximity in Oban, reportedly linked to potent heroin which may have been sourced in West Dumbartonshire.
Death and multiple overdoses reportedly linked to street benzos in the area which are potent, including etizolam, clonazolam and bromazolam.
Multiple hospitalisations for individuals reporting side effects from semaglutide accessed without a prescription.
Report to service that 'monkey dust' is becoming more common as it is cheaper than crack.

Reports of multiple people taking 'Ksalol/Quesos/Keysos'. Branded as Galenika Ksalols 1mg tablets and sold as alprazolam and Xanax. Suspected to contain benzos and synthetic opioids. One person reports taking two tablets and feeling a significant numbing effect. Naloxone was not fully effective in reversing overdose.
Multiple overdoses across different age groups related to Xanax.
Blue tablets sold as diazepam (Accord, half score on one side), were sent to testing by WEDINOS. Results shown bromazolam and metonitazene.

Adverse effects including unconsciousness, breathlessness and irregular heartbeat after smoking and injecting heroin. WEDINOS testing detected heroin, N-desethyl etonitazene, paracetamol and caffeine. This is the first known detection of N-desethyl etonitazene in Scotland.

Post-mortem testing in a death from multidrug intoxication detected desalkylgidazepam, a metabolite of gidazepam and a drug in its own right. This is the first known detection of this drug in a death in this area.
Alert issued by Food Standards Agency due to sale of counterfeit 35cl bottles of Glen's vodka found to contain isopropyl alcohol in Glasgow and Lanarkshire.

Increased prevalence of small white benzo pills and people experiencing prolonged effects over several days after consumption, people who were 'out of it' and people who were covered in white powder from the tablets.

Tests of vapes were positive for bromazolam and spice. Substance being mis-sold as etizolam but having a much stronger/different effect on them. Reports of adverse effects including self-harming and seizures.
Reports of heightened effects from pills and vapes/cannabis. Effects are visibly apparent to those not under the influence.
Overdose after snorting what they thought was heroin. WEDINOS testing detected heroin, xylazine, metonitazene, noscapine, caffeine and paracetamol.

Multiple hospitalisations due to overdose. Clinical signs include altered conscious level, hyperglycaemia, airway compromise and inadequate breathing. Patients lived in wide geographical area. One overdose was in a park and white circular pills (stamped 'NFD' and half score on reverse, in medicinal packaging) branded alprazolam were found at the scene and have been sent for testing.
Concerns around adulterated cocaine in circulation.

Overdose (collapsed and unconsciousness) on the street. Patient had a bag of 150 mixed pills - white, chalky square tablets (marked with 'PR') said to be pregabalin and green round tablets (half score, no other markings) said to be street benzos. Patient said the benzos were 'rough and obviously a dodgy batch' so they were taking the pregabalin to take the edge off it.
Adverse effects including multiple seizures from taking street benzos stamped 'CDB'. Recently started taking benzos, using hundreds daily.

Patient on the street with adverse effects including hallucinations and paranoia after taking 'the new street Valium' (small, crumbly white pills, stamped 'C1') and 'synthetic cocaine' (rough white powder).
Price of heroin in area reported as dropping to £15 for a half gram (0.5g), from what was steadily £25 for 0.5g. Quality as 'middling not great but not terrible'. Delivered by dealer in 15 minutes.

Patient had difficulty walking due to swollen legs. They had discoloured skin and ulcerations around ankles and feet. Reported taking approximately 20 pregabalin and 200 benzos over the course of a day. The pills were green or yellow and described as 'quite big'.

Multiple people experienced adverse effects including an inability to stand, difficulty breathing, palpitations and chest tightness, after injecting half a score bag of heroin. It appeared 'unusually less brown' when heated, gave no high and they suspected it was 'cut with something bad'. No response to nasal naloxone. Effects worn off quickly. Substance sent for testing.
Overdose (unconscious, not breathing, irregular pulse) on a street after injecting heroin. Regained consciousness after one dose of naloxone. No memory of collapse.

Overdose (collapsed) on a street after taking two crack rocks and 150 street benzos over the course of a day. The pills were larger than normal green pills, sourced from a dealer. Patient had swollen painful legs and an open wound behind their knee which was inflamed and seeping.

Green powder and green tablets (no markings) causing adverse effects including aggression, difficulty breathing, unconsciousness, suicidal thoughts, vomiting, violence and self-harm after being snorted or vaped. Testing of tablets detected anabolic steroids.

Multiple overdoses a few hours apart where persons purchased what they believed was benzos. One person had also taken ketamine and alcohol. Adverse effects included blue lips, snoring, not responsive, heavy muscles and unable to move. Responsive to naloxone. Drugs found at scene include yellow and white capsules and a blister pack.

Adverse effects including jaw clenching, teeth grinding, pin-point pupils, lack of coordination, mania and agitation at festival after taking MDMA-type drugs. Behaviour was very 'up' and more stimulated than expected with MDMA. Sold as MDMA but reported was 'like a mix bag' with ecstasy, ketamine, stimulant effects all in one.

appearance: Orange pills, white pills, red pills
summary: Royal apples (tapentadol and carisoprodol mix) being sold in Lothian. If taking tapentadol on its own it is an orange tablet and the side effects include extreme dizziness which can last for up to an hour, so the carisoprodol (also known as soma) is taken to stop the dizziness. Often bought in blister packs via online messaging app.
Suspected drug death in park.
Detections of hexahydrocannabinol (HHC) in prisons. One in powder form and one in resin for (that also contained delta-8-THC).
Report from workers that young people are now taking 'party mix' - a mix of cocaine and ketamine.
Report of a death from multidrug toxicity where nitazenes were implicated without heroin or a benzodiazepine. Unknown green tablets found at scene of death.
Suspected drug death in person thought to have taken red apples (tapentadol and carisoprodol).

Person experiencing significant ulceration, seeping wounds on feet and amnesia with difficulty recalling the previous few days. Reported taking green street benzos and turquoise Xanax (sometimes white) for around three weeks.
Report of swollen wounds from intravenous heroin use. Reported they need to use more vit C to break it down, when previously only needed a pinch. Reports the effects being delayed but intense.
Adverse effects from substance purchased as diazepam with rough edges and half score on one side. Effects include 'wiping them out' and amnesia.
Overdose (respiratory arrest and immediate collapse) after snorting green crushed tablets. Bought online from UK dealer as 'nitazenes'.

Adverse effects experienced by more than one person from pregabalin purchased online. They experienced a histamine effect (allergic reaction) - swelling in lips, tongue and eyes lasting up to a day. Appeared to be 'normal' red/white 300 mg Lyrica pregabalin capsules in sealed strips with commercial branding.

Red apples in circulation in the Mid and East Lothian containing tapentadol and carisoprodol/somas. Can be sold separately or mixed as Rosie/Royal Apples 225mg combined tablets. If sold separately, tapentadol is larger sized orange tablet and carisoprodol is smaller sized white tablet. Adverse effects from tapentadol include dizziness.

Hospitalisation of person known to take heroin. Treated for hypothermia (low body temperature) and loss of consciousness. Pupils were pin point. Low response to naloxone. Concern that heroin was adulterated with xylazine.
Report of high strength heroin in circulation in Inverness and surrounding areas causing unconsciousness almost immediately. Multiple doses of naloxone administered and CPR performed.

Overdose in a club from swallowing MDMA pills. Adverse effects include hallucinations, hyperthermia (high body temperature), psychosis and tachycardia (high heart rate). The white pills had Teletech logo on one side, with 'hardcore never dies' on the reverse. Sent to WEDINOS for testing.
Client reports taking MDMA pills that were chocolate brown in colour with gold sparkles, called 'bad boy eccies/bunnies'.

Overdose behind retail unit after injecting half a £10 bag of heroin. It was an off-white course powder, sourced from a dealer and they believe it 'was not heroin'. Adverse effects include agitation, anxiety, confusion, difficulty breathing, nausea, hyperthermia (high body temperature), numbness, tingling and feelings of falling.

Overdose (collapse) in a public close after injecting a £5 bag of heroin (lighter in colour than usual) and swallowing five benzos. Adverse effects include agitation, collapse, anxiety, confusion, difficulty breathing, nausea, hypothermia (low body temperature), shaky and feeling numb. Found with needle in situ.
Use of propylhexedrine (nasal decongestant) mixed with other drugs to mimic the effects of cocaine. Referred to as 'prop'. Administered through injecting and snorting (resulting in sinus infection).

Overdose on the street. Adverse effects including anxiety, distress, difficulty breathing, hallucinations, pounding heart, chest pain and panic attack after injecting one gram of cocaine. Had also consumed alcohol and 10 street benzos.
Report of new drug called 'fools heroin' sold as heroin in loose brown pills.
Increase in adverse effects in prisons including long periods of blackouts/memory loss.
Increase in prison residents being placed on observation due to level of intoxication after vaping. Adverse effects include vomiting, tingling/numbness, felt out of body and unable to move.
Adverse effects for eight hours after injecting cocaine including fear, rapid heart rate and feeling like they were having a heart attack.
Death from necrotising fasciitis associated with drug use.
Increase in patients presenting with aspiration pneumonia after long periods of sedation.
Report that the heroin is being adulterated with buprenorphine to bulk it out. A few patients have tested positive for both heroin and buprenorphine.
Under 25s vaping substance thought to be THC, experienced adverse physical and mental effects resulting in hospitalisation.
Large brachial abscess and injection site in a 'very poor state' associated with injecting heroin/xylazine. This is the second case seen by the service with severe wounds.
Several people under 25 became sleepy and unwell after vaping a clear liquid, thought to contain THC.

Hospitalisation after smoking pink cocaine, also called tusi/tuci and many contain a combination of MDMA, morphine, ketamine and cocaine. Adverse effects include memory loss and feeling both physically and psychologically unwell.

A person died as a result of deep vein thrombosis and septic embolism (confirmed as different to patient in report 8-74). History of smoking crack cocaine and Valium and heroin consumption. Initial presentation was of non-specific symptoms including fatigue, sickness, stiff neck and high temperature.
Overdose and hospital admission after consumption of 100 street Valium and eight green Xanax.
Death of person due to possible DVT (deep vein thrombosis). Injected heroin and cocaine, occasional street Valium use and smoking of crack cocaine.
Substances tested by WEDINOS, sold as THC (tetrahydrocannabinol) or CBD (cannabidiol) vapes but contained spice (MDMB-4EN-PINACA, 5F-ABD, 4F-MDMB-BINACA).
Substance tested by WEDINOS, sold as heroin found to contain xylazine, paracetamol, heroin, metonitazene and bromazolam.

Four substances tested by WEDINOS sold as diazepam found to contain bromazolam and metonitazene in Scotland, with effects such as nausea, sweating, memory loss and agitation. Sold as blue diazepam tablets - branding included Martin Dow and Bensedin.
Drug sold as 'scab' heroin, reported to be stronger than usual.
Noticeable increase in the use of Xanax. Adverse effects include cognitive impairment, severe drowsiness and decreased mobility leading to falls.
Two amputations thought to be due to complications related to injecting.
Heroin less potent and requires more vitamin C to break down, reportedly people don't use heroin for effects now but to get rid of withdrawals.
Client overdosed after injecting 0.2g of heroin, which is a normal dose for them.
Reports of crack cocaine being mixed with other substances recently that are 'as bad as the heroin'.
Person who injected heroin reported a more potent but brief effect, and withdrawals happening faster.
Sustained increase in number of overdoses in Highland.

Greater Manchester Drugs Early Warning System issued alert in June about ketamine adulterated with xylazine, after several tests in Manchester on samples of drugs sold as ketamine detected the presence of xylazine.
Multiple overdoses and reports of increased harm including reduced consciousness, linked to street benzos and opioids. Overdose reports also noting use of 'Arabic diazepam' and illicit amitriptyline.
Green Xanax linked to overdose.
Increase in cocaine-related harms including cocaine being implicated in a high number of drug deaths, an increase in crack cocaine use, and an increase in septum/soft nasal tissue damage.
Stimulant/amphetamine-like effects after swallowing pills bought as street benzos/Xanax. Testing was positive for amphetamines.
Suspected drug deaths are relatively high for the area. High number of detections of bromazolam in death reports.
Information from injecting assessments show a majority of people injecting cocaine, and many people smoking crack cocaine. Reported reduction in use of benzodiazepines and heroin.
Increasing demand for 'prop' cocaine, resulting in decline in availability of poorer quality cocaine.
Report that heroin is poor quality right now, which increases the likelihood of adulteration e.g. nitazene for the psychoactive effect and xylazine as a bulking agent.
Significant proportion of positive cases of nitazenes in Scotland over the last year were detected in the north east.
Workers noting an increase in reports of ketamine use in young people across the city.

Multiple overdoses and hospitalisations after taking pink heroin, white pills (stamped '10C') and pregabalin. Time between consumption and overdose was very quick. Other adverse effects include disorientation, confusion and extreme drowsiness.
Anecdotal reports of stronger heroin with some people taking harm reduction steps to reduce consumption and use with others around.
Adverse effects including loss of consciousness and respiratory issues linked to ADB-BUTINACA powder, recovered in prisons.

Substances sold as diazepam sent to WEDINOS. Results varied - most contained either bromazolam or etizolam, one contained phenacetin ('magic') and one contained bromazolam and metonitazene. Appearance varied but most were blue colour with 'MSJ' stamped on one side, much smaller than genuine diazepam.
Reports of pink heroin that is stronger than usual.
Multiple deaths linked to heroin. Some experienced immediate loss of consciousness after injecting or snorting. Xylazine was found to be present in samples taken.
Drug-related deaths commonly found to involve bromazolam, heroin, cocaine and etizolam. Cocaine is one of the most common substances found in post-mortem toxicology.
Prison testing found bromazolam on paper tabs. Reports of severe intoxication from small dose.
Adverse effect of methemoglobinemia after taking cocaine.
Increase in use of ketamine by young people, usually recovered alongside other drugs like MDMA and LSD.
Increase in the use of THC vapes but limited testing data available.
Multiple overdoses from heroin use. Reports of 'strong heroin' circulating. At least a full 2mg naloxone was used to reverse overdose.
Report of detections of desalkylgidazepam in post-mortem toxicology (alongside cocaine, and cocaine and bromazolam).
Multiple overdoses from suspected heroin/nitazene use. Reports of new county line in operation in the area.
Adverse effects requiring hospitalisation in people under 25, including feeling sick and light headed, after taking ketamine.
Adverse effects including unconsciousness and difficulty breathing after taking diazepam/Valium. Effects improved after naloxone.
Adverse effects including hallucinations and overdose after consuming unknown tablets.
Adverse effects including amnesia, hallucinations, psychosis, unusual behaviour and cardiac arrhythmia.
Patient unwell after smoking crack cocaine in early evening, with ambulance called at midnight. Adverse effects of anxiety/panic, chest pain, numbness and pins and needles in left arm.
Patient injected heroin and lost consciousness for several hours. Reported they 'knew it wasn't right'.
Patient overdosed and had an extended period of intoxication after injecting heroin. Other adverse effects include itching.
Patient had adverse effects including chest pain and felt like they 'were going to have a heart attack' after injecting crack cocaine in hand. Also noted swelling at injecting site.
Patient had adverse effects including wounds and numb forearm after injecting heroin. Described it as 'feeling like novocaine'.
Patient with wound injuries requiring surgery after injecting. Stated substance sold as cocaine is congealing.
Adverse effects including seizures and overdose after taking powder cocaine (batches sold as prop and council).
Multiple drug deaths in the one area. No known link. Reports of high levels of deprivation.
Multiple overdoses in people aged under 25 in separate locations, needing ambulance service after collapse. Reports of ketamine, alcohol and heroin.
Ambulance attendance and hospitalisation for adverse effects including collapse, in multiple people aged under 25, after consuming THC vape.
Suspected drug death, person found wearing fentanyl patch.
Post-mortem toxicology detected protonitazene, metonitazene and xylazine. Cause of death was multidrug intoxication.
Positive test results from nitazene testing strips in drugs sold as diazepam, heroin and cocaine.
General increase in cannabis extract products, including synthetics (spice).

Incidents involving young people experiencing severe breathing difficulties after using vapes. Reported buying vapes via social media that may contain spice or other drugs as they're cheaper than THC vapes. One incident where a young person's overdose responded to naloxone.
Recoveries from a festival mainly included packets of white powder and the purchase intent was MDMA. Effects included increased heart rate, jaw and legs shaking, anxiety and dilated pupils.
Seizure of cannabis plants linked to organised crime.
Tablets sold as Xanax bars found to contain bromazolam and clonazolam.

Cocaine use has increased among people usually taking heroin or other opioids. Overall use has increased across the population in all forms. Increased injection of cocaine, and risk of wounds and infections.
Increased dominance of xylazine as an additive to heroin. Recently seized block containing predominantly xylazine. No fentanyl present in any recoveries.
Services report an increase in people admitted to hospital for near fatal overdose.
Reports of adverse effects after consuming cannabis thought to be adulterated with spice.
Vapes thought to contain spice resulting in adverse effects including impaired thinking, slowed speech, hallucinations and unconsciousness.
Report of street benzo, described as 'really strong' and called 'dynamite'. Stating that the extended effects last up to two days. Nitazene testing strip showing negative for nitazenes.
Synthetic cannabinoids detected in crystal form.

Service started providing nitazene rapid response testing strips. Test on heroin sample was positive for nitazene. Felt the effects were different to usual feeling after using heroin with increased negative effects and sickness.
Increase in people under 25 presenting with adverse mental health effects after using cannabis or cannabis products.
Counterfeit Ksalol (brand for alprazolam) in circulation.

Adverse effect of methemoglobinemia after snorting cocaine several times in the last week. No change reported to the usual appearance or supplier of the batch. Other people also had taken the same source but did not experience this.
Adverse effects including collapse after taking cocaine. Person had pinpoint pupils and was given naloxone which had no effect.
Overdose with features of opioid involvement (pinpoint pupils and responsive to naloxone) in a person with no reported history of opioid consumption (pregabalin, street benzodiazepines and cannabis).
Adverse effects after use of THC/spice vape including slower physical reactions in movement and speech, altered mental health, hallucinations and psychosis.
Reports of bacterial infections in blood and soft tissues, deep vein thrombosis and endocarditis in people who take drugs.
Adverse effects from cocaine and heroin, potentially adulterated.
Young people using THC vape, difficult to detect due to no smell.
Substance sold as liquid THC being injected. THC crystals being smoked via a pipe (similar to a crack pipe). Effects include hours of hallucinations.
Individual reported concerns with their heroin including it being thick and congeals easily. Also has leg ulcer.
Sudden adverse effects including anxiety and confusion soon after taking diazepam/Valium pills stamped 'MSJ' on one side, half score on the reverse. Yellow and blue coloured.
New drug, pink powder named 'pink cocaine, tuci, tusi or tucibi'. Contents are variable but include a mixture of cocaine, MDMA or other drugs.
Heroin reportedly cut with fentanyl making people feel unwell. Not confirmed by toxicology.
High strength cocaine powder in area.
Suspected adulterated benzodiazepine/alprazolam.
Adverse effects reported after taking MDMA pill including anxiety, confusion, depression and aggression.
High strength Valium reported.
Several individuals reporting adverse effects for several weeks after using 'street Valium', including extreme paranoia, violence subjected on others and anxiety.
Drug-related death. Purchase intent was heroin with fentanyl but post-mortem testing confirmed metonitazene, protonitazene, bromazolam and xylazine.
Seizures and other adverse effects associated with unmarked white pills.
Death associated with unmarked white benzo pills, causing cardiac arrest.
Increased number of adolescents presenting with psychotic symptoms. It was believed that most have used some sort of cannabis.
'Fake Ksalol' (benzodiazepine) tablets in circulation in Scotland. Contents have been variable.
Methemoglobinemia reported in a patient who had snorted cocaine.
Reports of 'crystal spice' in circulation in England.
New drug reported in prison called 'fish' or 'fish tranquilisers', powder that is smoked. Adverse effects include sudden collapse.
Several non-fatal overdoses following reports of smoking substances, possibly thought to be synthetic cannabinoids. Other effects include seizures, dizziness, disorientation and unusual behaviour.
Several near fatal and fatal overdoses reportedly connected to smoking or injecting crack cocaine and heroin.
Crack cocaine reportedly contributed towards multiple people experiencing seizures or hospitalisation. Powder reported as yellow/brown in colour and when cooked up, turned green.
Young people reporting 'rhino ket'. High potency. With possible makeup of MXE (methoxetamine). Adverse effects include mouth ulcers and heart palpitations.
Strong heroin, brick red colour in circulation. Reports that people wanted to take more after a short period of time. Also strong pills, potentially Xanax bars in circulation.
Brown powder sold as heroin giving unexpected effects. Several samples tested by WEDINOS found to contain xylazine and nitazenes, as well as heroin.
Significant skin infections and wounds in people who use drugs.
Harms involving bromazolam, nitazenes and etizolam reported in prison. Increased vaping of waxy substances in oil, including benzodiazepines.

Reported feedback from people who have taken nitazenes include: a different burn, sudden collapse after consumption, different colours. When prepared for injection, the substance can block needles and turn jelly-like. Leaves reported green, purple, pinkish or sand colour residue on equipment.
Overdose of tapentadol. Suspected source was mail order from India.
Xylazine detected via WEDINOS samples in areas across the UK, including Lothian, Forth Valley and the Borders.
Report of 'tis squares' card that has been dipped in etizolam in both prison and community.
'Prescribed MSJ' tablets described as being potent and likely to cause negative side effects, including near fatal overdose.
'Fish tranquilisers' reportedly in circulation in prison.
Methamphetamine mis-sold as MDMA.
Deaths involving cocaine and methadone increased from last year. Young people reporting ketamine use, and potent THC vapes in circulation.
Several local reports of cocaine and ketamine use in young people, with adverse health consequences.
Several young people experienced adverse health consequences reportedly due to consumption of black Maserati ecstasy pills.
A new opiate tea called 'tizzy tea'. Said to originate in prisons and 'quickly gaining popularity' due to the high potency and the ease with which you can obtain it.
'Scab' heroin circulating. Reportedly potent and cheap.
Green Xanax circulating known as 'hulk Xanax', reportedly potent.
Death of young person. Reported as having taken a pill shortly before becoming unwell, thought to be ecstasy.
Patches of tissue necrosis [injury/death] in multiple people who inject cocaine, with no evidence or reports of missed shots.

Grey heroin, reported to be 'stronger' than brown and imported from Pakistan. Smoked 0.2 grams and was 'out' for hours, experiencing vivid dreams and blackouts. Concern about people who inject due to intensity.
Concern about crushing diazepam tablets and mixing it with heroin to inject.
Potent Valium tablets being sold. Harder than usual in texture.
'Bad batch' of Valium causing overdose and serious adverse effects.
Reports of mixing ketamine and cocaine and increasing use of ketamine in young people.
Multiple suspected drug deaths.
Patient admitted to hospital with cocaine-induced choreoathetosis [involuntary movements]. Same symptoms also reported that week in another area.
Hospitalisation and seizures after taking energy drink powder (reconstituted with water).
Multiple suspected drug deaths.
Xylazine detected in a death, alongside benzos, nitazenes and heroin. Person was reported to have taken 'crocodile' from Russia/Ukraine.
Adverse effects including overdose and death linked to an unknown substance called 'krokodil'.
Adverse effects including overdose linked to the use of liquid cocaine in spray bottles.
Pink 'tusi' powder, sold for £100 per gram. Advertised as containing MDMA, ketamine and caffeine.

Reports of white heroin that's 'not very strong'. Described as hard, difficult to breakdown and sticky consistency once burned. Effects described as 'gouching' but keeps you awake. Reports of fentanyl in circulation.
Reports of carisoprodol tablets ('red apples') in circulation. Sold online in red and light yellow/beige packaging branded with 'Royal 225'.
Xylazine in sample alongside heroin. Detected by WEDINOS.

Adverse effects including decreased energy and extreme sedation after swallowing tapentadol and carisoprodol pill (also called 'red apples'). Taken alongside benzos, crack cocaine and methadone. Sold in gold/bronze foil blister packets branded with picture of three red apples and 'Royal 225'.

Multiple reports from service users that for the last month or so there has been higher strength heroin available. People reported they had cut the amount they used - taking half a £10 bag, injected or vaped from foil.
Detection of metonitazene in a death (alongside benzos, cocaine, methadone and heroin/morphine).
Increasing reports of crack cocaine and injecting.
Orange powder or crystals of bromazolam. Adverse effects include extreme sedation, nausea and vomiting - resulting in aspiration pneumonia.

Multiple people in housing/homeless service reporting adverse effects from injecting crack cocaine (prop) including a 'banging' headache/migraine. The drug was crystallising (or recrystallising) on the spoon after dissolved for injecting. Cost £200 for 3.5 grams.
Overdoses linked to baby blues (street benzos thought to contain bromazolam).

Blue pills in medical looking blister packaging sold as benzos, branded 'Ksalol', suspected alprazolam (Xanax). Adverse effects after swallowing pills: amnesia (memory loss), decreased energy, depression/low mood, difficulty breathing and hallucinations.
Methamphetamine vaped/smoked from a glass pipe. Sourced from England from a friend.

'Strong' white/cream heroin which doesn't dissolve well and was not clear when heated for injection. Immediate effects: euphoria, heightened senses and pins and needles. After effects: feeling physically awful and 'stoned' for days.
Adverse effects including overdose and extreme sedation after swallowing multiple 'red apples' (carisoprodol and tapentadol).
Reports of 'strong' black heroin 'knocking people out' and leaving residue in spoons. Querying synthetic opioid contamination (not confirmed by tox).
Service reports people taking 'somas' in multiple premises. Sample was sent to WEDINOS and was found to contain carisoprodol and codeine.
Reports of young people using 'chalkies' thought to be benzos, sold 100 pills for £100. Also using alongside crack cocaine.

appearance: Black waxy substance, blue pills, white pills
summary: Inpatient found with black sticky/waxy substance and street benzos. White pills were marked with half-score and 'Roche 10' and blue pills were marked with half-score and '10'. Adverse effects include amnesia (memory loss), confusion, decreased energy, depression/low mood, hallucinations, psychosis and oversedation.
Reports of continued availability and use of mephedrone.
Reports that the heroin/nitazene substance that caused overdoses in Dublin, is circulating in Belfast. Testing in Ireland confirmed substance to be N-pyrrolidino protonitazene - no heroin detected.

Vaping of 'monkey paws' powder in prisons, believed to be powdered etizolam [since suspected to be bromazolam - the most common benzo powder detected by prison drug analysis]. Onset was 30 minutes and effects lasted for hours. Adverse effects after four puffs of a vape: amnesia (loss of memory), nausea and vomiting and extreme sedation. After effects: no recollection of the rest of the day and still 'out of it' the next day.
Reports of fentanyl being sold (not confirmed by tox).
Hospitalisation of person under 25.
People filming themselves taking drugs and being under the influence for social media.

UK-wide drug trends from festivals shared by national welfare support organisation include: significant increase in ketamine across UK (often mixed with alcohol); MDMA (pills and powders) is the second most common substance reported; orange Tesla and peach Supreme tablets positive for 4-CMC [cathinone, stimulant] - contained no MDMA; multiple cases of young people unwell after taking 2-CB; tusi/pink cocaine also circulating.
Suspected drug death linked to polydrug use.
Adverse effects after swallowing pills, multiple overdoses in the same time period. Suspected to contain metonitazene and bromazolam as a similar substance was tested by WEDINOS.
